decision.summary: 31 of 31 findings are evidence-backed; 0 were insufficient and recorded for follow-up.

findings.statement: NVIDIA's public data‑center materials describe a portfolio involving accelerated compute, systems, networking, and software.
NVIDIA describes system‑level offerings under the DGX platform.
NVIDIA's software ecosystem includes CUDA and AI software offerings.
NVIDIA's public data‑center portfolio is broader than a single accelerator.
NVIDIA data‑center product portfolio is listed at https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/.
Data‑center system is evaluated as a complete bill of materials and supported configuration.
Performance and utilization across training, fine‑tuning, and inference workloads are key evaluation criteria.
Supply lead times and eligibility must be validated for the exact product configuration and destination.
Broadcom disclosed six AI customers for its custom XPU accelerators, explicitly naming Google, Meta Platforms, OpenAI and Anthropic, with two additional hyperscalers remaining undisclosed.

Broadcom's custom AI chips are priced at $13,000 per TPU chip for Google projects and $5,000 per chip for other projects; cloud pricing for the Ironwood TPU is $12.00 per chip‑hour on demand and $5.40 per chip‑hour on a three‑year commitment.

Broadcom reported AI semiconductor revenue of $8.4 B in Q1 FY26, $10.8 B in Q2 FY26, $16.7 B in Q3 FY26 and guided $21.7 B for Q4 FY26, resulting in $58 B AI revenue for FY26. The company projects $115 B AI revenue in FY27 and $230 B in FY28, and estimates $30 B of annual recurring revenue per gigawatt of deployed compute.
Broadcom reports that more than 1,000 business customers are each spending at least $1 million annually on its AI‑related products.
Broadcom’s FY 2024 total revenue was $51.6 billion, of which AI‑related semiconductor revenue reached $10 billion (35 % of total). Q1 2025 revenue was $14.9 billion.

Intel Corp: Intel disclosed that its Gaudi AI accelerator portfolio will not meet the $500 million revenue target for 2024, falling short of the previously stated $1‑2 billion goal. The Q3 2024 earnings report confirmed Gaudi revenue is below $500 million for the year.

Broadcom lists its VMware VCF subscription at $200–$400 per core per year for typical mid‑market customers, and its VVF subscription at $100–$200 per core per year. For Symantec Endpoint Security, Broadcom lists a mid‑market price of $30–$60 per endpoint per year.
Benchmark posts claim AMD MI300X provides 2.4× more memory capacity and 1.6× higher bandwidth than Nvidia H100, highlighting a perceived performance advantage for AMD among some AI developers.
NVIDIA promotes its A100 Tensor Core GPU as delivering up to 20× higher performance over the prior generation, reflecting strong positive messaging about performance among cloud providers.
Vultr announced a 20 MW AMD AI supercluster deployment in India, indicating significant adoption of AMD GPUs by a cloud service provider.
NVIDIA A100 GPUs are listed for up to $22,000 on retail sites, suggesting high acquisition cost that may deter some cloud operators or AI developers.
Fireworks AI states that it offers Llama inference using both Nvidia and AMD GPUs, suggesting developers view both vendors as viable for inference workloads.
US hyperscalers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft) plan to deploy over 5 million AI training‑capable accelerators in 2024, indicating strong demand from cloud service providers.
Revenue for AI accelerators (GPUs and custom accelerators) surged 130 % in Q3 2024, reflecting rapid adoption and escalating market demand.

The overall AI accelerator market is expanding rapidly, as evidenced by NVIDIA’s data‑center revenue rising from $15 billion in 2022 to over $100 billion in 2024 and projected above $130 billion in 2025.
NVIDIA H100 inference costs $0.09 per million tokens for GPT-OSS-120B at 66 TPS/user using vLLM, indicating its price-performance baseline in the AI accelerator market.
NVIDIA B200 inference costs $0.02 per million tokens for GPT-OSS-120B at 55 TPS/user using TensorRT‑LLM, making it roughly 4.5× cheaper than the H100 and highlighting a competitive pricing advantage.
US hyperscalers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft) plan to deploy over 5 million AI training‑capable accelerators in 2024, indicating strong demand from cloud service providers.
Current waiting times for cutting‑edge AI accelerators are around six months, highlighting supply constraints amid accelerating demand.
Broadcom targets a $60‑90 billion ASIC opportunity by 2027, indicating a strategic roadmap toward custom AI accelerator silicon that could erode GPU share in inference workloads.
NVIDIA H100 inference costs about $0.09 per million tokens for GPT-OSS-120B using vLLM, indicating its price-performance baseline in the AI accelerator market.

NVIDIA B200 inference costs about $0.02 per million tokens for GPT-OSS-120B using TensorRT‑LLM, roughly 4.5× cheaper than H100, showing a significant cost reduction trend for newer NVIDIA accelerators.

EU enterprises need AI‑specific Data Processing Agreement (DPA) addenda that explicitly cover inference data handling, deletion timelines, and sub‑processor disclosures when using cloud inference APIs for regulated workloads.
